plan.topic: Queasy the morning after Thanksgiving dinner on tirzepatide: is that normal, and when to call
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Queasy the day after Thanksgiving on tirzepatide? Nausea is a common side effect on its label.' Card by 6 s: 'Nausea: 28% on top dose vs 8% placebo · adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes · Zepbound label pool, up to 72 weeks · adverse reactions'. Then the exact escalation sentence. Separate sentence: 'Tirzepatide also slows how fast your stomach empties.' Tips, with no guilt and no making up for the meal: 'Small, bland portions when hunger returns.' 'Sip fluids, unless you've been told to limit fluids.' Then 'Contact your prescriber if you can't keep fluids down.', the tirzepatide emergency card ('with or without vomiting … right away'), the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Don't use 'mostly'. Leave out the 53% figure.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide: Queasy the Morning After Thanksgiving? #shorts
plan.why: Last day of the holiday slot. Day-after felt-symptom Shorts are proven (full the morning after 497, stomach pain 271), and day-after nausea hasn't been covered yet. | fact-check: Confirmed in the Zepbound PI at uspl.lilly.com/zepbound/zepbound.html. The sentence 'The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.' is real. Table 2 is the pool of Study 1 and Study 2 in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes. Nausea: 28% at 15 mg vs 8% on placebo (29% at 10 mg, so call 15 mg 'the top dose' and don't call it 'the highest rate'). Those are label adverse-reaction figures, so the card says 'adverse reactions'. Date conflict: that page prints 'Revised: 8/2026', but the craft notes give Zepbound DailyMed as 16 Nov 2026. Cite the date of the exact document you link. Two framing risks. First, Thanksgiving is the setting: don't say the meal caused the nausea. Second, write 'tirzepatide delays gastric emptying' as its own sentence and don't present it as the cause. Table 2 comes from Zepbound's weight trials, so name that scope on the card. Today is the slot's last day (Thanksgiving was 26 Nov), so it must ship tonight or be dropped.

package.title: Tirzepatide: Queasy the Morning After Thanksgiving? #shorts
package.description:
Nausea is a common side effect on tirzepatide's label. In Zepbound's weight trials, it was an adverse reaction for 28% of adults on 15 mg vs 8% on placebo. The label says the majority of nausea, vomiting or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.
Contact your prescriber if you cannot keep fluids down. If you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without vomiting, stop using tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta: Spoken close, in order: the fixed don't-stop line ('For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.'), then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then the loop line 'Back to the morning after.' No subscribe line and no 'link in the description'. POST NOTES: I counted the spoken words myself: 157 ('twenty-eight' counts as one word; 158 if it counts as two). Standard arm, about 68 s. Narration is the same as the fact-checked draft. Only on-screen text, the s2 card fact, the s6 retention note and the s6 source tag changed. Exp G target long video: Thanksgiving (holiday → Thanksgiving). Last day of the holiday slot: ship tonight or drop it. Cite S1 at the PI page's printed 'Revised: 8/2026'. Cite S2 at the DailyMed Medication Guide's 'Revised: 11/2026' (SPL effective 16 Nov 2026). If the S2 set ID doesn't open to the Zepbound Medication Guide, swap in the working DailyMed URL for that same document and keep its own date. The fluids caveat ('unless you've been told to limit fluids'), the 'can't keep fluids down' line and the safety lines are our own wording and carry no source tags. s6 is tagged S2 for the pancreatitis wording only. Motion: s1, s2 and s3 cards are longer than usual (fact-checker muted-viewer fixes), so split each into whole clauses of 2 lines or fewer and never end a card on a comma or colon. On-screen numbers are digits and always 'type 2', never 'TYPE TWO'. The don't-stop line is exactly two cards: 'FOR ANYTHING THAT ISN'T THAT EMERGENCY SIGN' / 'DON'T STOP OR CHANGE YOUR MEDICINE ON YOUR OWN.' 'NOT PERSONAL ADVICE, SO ASK YOUR PRESCRIBER.' is one card.

factcheck.summary: The core claims match the sources. The Zepbound prescribing information page prints "Revised: 8/2026". Its Table 2 shows nausea at 28% on 15 mg vs 8% on placebo (2,519 adults with obesity or overweight, up to 72 weeks). The dose-escalation sentence is word for word: "The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time." Section 12.2 says "Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying." The Medication Guide's pancreatitis wording matches s6: stop and call your healthcare provider right away for severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without vomiting. The NHS page (last reviewed 17 Nov 2023) supports smaller meals, regular sips of a cold drink, and avoiding strong-smelling, hot, fried or greasy food. DailyMed confirms the set ID is Zepbound, SPL effective 16 Nov 2026. I couldn't extract the Medication Guide's own printed "Revised: 11/2026" date from the PDF; it matches the channel's known date, so I've kept it. Thanksgiving is the setting, not the cause. The safety lines are correct, with "that emergency sign" since only one sign is named. The spoken word count is 157, which matches the post notes and fits the standard arm. There are no dosing or stopping instructions. Only minor wording and muted-viewer fixes are needed.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits well under the voice already (-13.5 dB) but ran a touch hot in pauses (-11.7 vs ~-14 target), so I pulled the overall bed down ~2 dB; speech-bed lands near -15.8 (slightly under the floor but close) while pauses settle near -13.6. For cues: thinned out simultaneous duplicate pairs (swell+whoosh, pop+whip, pop+whoosh, pop+tick, swell+whoosh) by keeping the one that matches the shot's named transition/mood and quieting its twin, rather than dropping either outright, to avoid clutter while keeping some texture. Boosted the badly buried swell/tick under the "brand" fade at 21.8s and the stat-reveal swell/tick at 8.4s (both were 15-20 dB under voice, well outside the felt range) up toward the speech-SFX window; the 21.8s pair is capped at 1.5x and still runs a bit low because the source level was extremely quiet. Reduced a few cues that were running louder than the speech ceiling (-11 to -13 dB) back into the -14 to -20 dB felt zone. Added three medically-safe custom accents (kitchen ambience for the cozy hook, a bright chime on the 28%-vs-8% stat, and a closing chime swell) with no device/medicine imagery.
